title: Comparative evaluation of graphite-based cathode materials for autotrophic nitrate reduction and dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium in bioelectrochemical systems
content: Bioelectrochemical systems (BES) offer a promising approach for sustainable nitrate reduction and dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium (DNRA) selectivity; however, cathode material and architecture can affect reactor performance and product distribution. In this study, four graphite-based cathode materials (graphite felt, graphite granules, graphite rod, and graphite foil) were compared under identical operating conditions in autotrophic nitrate-reducing BES. Nitrate reduction rates ranged from 1.3 to 2.8 g NO3− per m−2 per day. Graphite felt and rod achieved the highest rates (2.7 and 2.8 g NO3− per m−2 per day), whereas graphite granules reached an intermediate rate (1.7 g NO3− per m−2 per day) and graphite foil the lowest rate (1.3 g NO3− per m−2 per day). Graphite felt and granules showed little to negligible nitrite accumulation, whereas pronounced nitrite accumulation occurred with graphite rod and foil. Coulombic efficiency and DNRA selectivity were high for all materials except graphite foil. Controls showed substantially lower nitrate reduction and no ammonium formation. Higher biofilm densities were associated with greater charge transfer during nitrate reduction and generally lower charge-transfer resistance. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) further indicated material/structure-dependent differences in the low-frequency impedance response, with weaker diffusion-related signatures for the 3D materials suggesting lower mass-transport resistance that may have contributed to reduced nitrite accumulation. Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) analysis was unsuitable for reliably comparing the specific surface areas of the investigated materials. Overall, the results indicate associations between cathode material properties, including architecture, biofilm development, electrochemical characteristics, and nitrate reduction performance and product distribution, with graphite felt and granules showing particularly promising characteristics.
